thought.text: The board was terminated after "Successfully ran target serve" — this is the standard Vite stdin-EOF behavior (when stdin is closed, the dev server exits. Since I redirected stdin to `/dev/null`, all three dev servers are exposed to this. app and cms were just probed first before being stopped by `just up` after the board terminated). The containers are healthy and data seeding is complete. The fix is to restart the dev server with stdin kept open, which is exactly what the documented `just serve` recipe is for.

reasoning_content:
The board's dev server is reporting "NX Successfully ran target serve for project urboards" (exit code 0), but before responding to the port, the process terminated. The Vite dev server is running in watch mode, so it shouldn't exit. The issue is probably that when running in the background without a TTY (detached, `setsid nohup ... < /dev/null`), Vite's watch mode exits because stdin was closed — Vite exits when stdin closes in non-interactive mode (this is known behavior: Vite exits if stdin closes, in order to support running in CI).

Actually, this is well-known Vite behavior: the dev server watches stdin, and when stdin closes (EOF), it terminates. In `just up`'s normal interactive usage, stdin is a TTY so the server keeps running. When I redirected stdin to /dev/null, Vite detected EOF on stdin and exited cleanly (code 0).

This is a byproduct of how I'm running it in the background, not a product defect. The board's process exited with code 0 after a successful build — the "NX Successfully ran target serve" confirms the build succeeded, and the process was terminated by the stdin EOF.

How to fix it: run the dev server with stdin held open (e.g., `< /dev/zero`? No, that streams zeros... actually Vite only exits on EOF; `tail -f /dev/null |` keeps stdin open). The simplest thing is: run `just serve` with stdin attached to a pipe that stays open, or use `setsid nohup just serve < <(sleep infinity)`? Hmm, process substitution with setsid...

Better approach: keep stdin open with `tail -f /dev/null | just serve`. Or just run `just up` again — since the containers are already up and the dev server will restart. The board's stdin will have the same problem though.

Wait — did the app and cms servers survive? They were reported "ready". But they have the same stdin-EOF condition. Maybe Vite only exits when stdin is *closed* AND there's no TTY... app and cms were probed as ready, so they were alive at that point. It's possible all three eventually exit on stdin EOF, but app and cms just happened to have responded first.

Actually, the Vite stdin-exit behavior: Vite's dev server has a `listen` option, and by default... let me try to recall: Vite watches `process.stdin` and calls `close` when stdin emits 'end'. This has been in Vite since around v3. The condition is: when not a TTY (i.e., in pipe mode). So yes — app and cms would also exit when their stdin is closed. They happened to respond before that... but wait, their stdin was also /dev/null (closed). Hmm, did they exit later? The message said "Stopping the rest and exiting with an error" — so just up killed them when the board crashed.

So, to get a fully working state with all three dev servers, I need to keep stdin open. Options:
1. `just up` again with stdin held open: `setsid nohup just up < <(sleep 100000)` — the process-substitution sleep keeps the pipe open.
2. Or, run `just serve` (the documented recipe for restarting the dev servers against an already-running instance) with stdin held open.

The containers are up and seeded; the guide says `just serve` brings the dev servers back. Let's run `just serve` with stdin held open.

One caveat though: the seed markers etc. are all fine. Re-running `just up` would re-execute the container steps (converging), and also start the dev servers. `just serve` is exactly designed for this: "Starts just the three dev servers against an already-running instance." Let's use `just serve` with stdin held open.

Also a note on `resolveSeedDecision`: `just serve` doesn't deal with the database, no problem.
